DEC-262 (a10), the ruling for 2b part 1, as relayed by the leader (opum-doc, option A, verbatim): Walk the chain: every symlink hop from the resolved tpm2_* to the final regular file (lstat per hop; a relative target resolves against its link's directory), the final file, and every ancestor directory of each hop and of the file, up to /. Each element must be owned by uid 0 or the invoking uid and must not be group- or other-writable. A sticky bit does NOT excuse a world-writable directory. On failure, refuse by name before spawning. Suggested code tpm2_tool_untrusted; ward-cli names it. The message carries the tool path, the first offending element with its owner and mode, and the remedy. NEVER fall through to a later PATH entry. Spawn unchanged: by the resolved tpm2_* path, not the realpath (argv[0] multicall). Keep statSync for the executable check. Tests both ways. Accept: a symlinked tpm2_create pointing at a multicall target in a 0755 tree. Reject: a group-writable PATH directory ahead of the good one; a world-writable sticky directory; a good link to a target in a writable directory; another uid's file.

THE LEADER'S TEST-SEAM GUARDRAILS (last message, verbatim in substance): Injecting trusted uids and the owner lookup through host options is acceptable as a TEST SEAM, with these guardrails: 1. The production default must read the real owner and mode from lstat/stat. Production callers must not be able to widen the trusted set. Make the seam narrow and clearly test-only. 2. Exercise the real default path with real files too: a tree you own with no group/other write passes, and a group- or other-writable ancestor or hop is refused (chmod, no chown needed). A root-owned real ancestor such as /usr should pass on the real path. 3. Name the injection in the PR body. Before the PR, check that the refusal reason lands in the Tpm2Reason union and the remedies Record.
WHERE #308 STANDS AGAINST THOSE (the leader's message crossed with my PR, so check): the refusal reason is tool_untrusted, not tpm2_tool_untrusted (named in the PR body as a choice; it is in the Tpm2Reason union and the remedies Record). The seams are Tpm2Host.trustedUids and Tpm2Host.trustRoot, both optional and unset in production (root plus the invoking user; walk to /); the PR body names them. Guardrail 1: the walk reads real owner and mode from lstat; BUT trustedUids is a public host option, so a production caller COULD widen the trusted set: review this, and consider making the seam test-only (a separate exported test entry point, or removing trustedUids and keeping only trustRoot) before the review round. Guardrail 2: the real default path is exercised by walking /bin/sh from / (root-owned ancestors, symlinks on Linux) and by chmod-built trees under trustRoot (group-writable dir, sticky 1777 dir set with chmod(1) because Bun chmodSync drops the sticky bit, group-writable file, writable link-target directory); there is no test of a tree walked from / with no trustRoot that the test owns (impossible: /tmp is sticky world-writable on Linux), so that part of guardrail 2 rests on trustRoot. One deviation to expect review on: a symlink is checked for owner only, since Linux reports every symlink as 0777.

ENVIRONMENT AND METHOD. Prefix every Bash call with: export PATH=$HOME/.nvm/versions/node/v24.22.2/bin:$PATH; (DEC-266). Run gh pr merge, git push and git merge each BARE in its own call (a composed or piped command is refused; a hook refuses a push joined to anything), with --match-head-commit and a literal SHA; gh pr merge --delete-branch also fast-forwards local dev and deletes the local branch. A hook rejects shell-variable write targets: use literal paths. Quest writes use --actor ward-cli-worker --actor-kind delegated-agent --accountable-human jdnewhouse; quest task complete moves the record to .quest/completed/, so git add the whole .quest/ dir; a task must be In Progress before complete. Tracker-only PRs land the usual way (task on dev first for an SDLC branch; wait for all three checks; merge bare). A mutation check is part of the proof: mutate the CHECK and confirm the predicted subset goes red, restore byte-for-byte (cmp against a scratchpad copy); a mutation that hangs a blocking open needs a deadline in the test. Bun quirks measured: chmodSync drops the sticky bit (use chmod(1)); Bun.spawn passes only the descriptors in stdio, even a dup'd fd without close-on-exec is not inherited. Reasoning rules from the leader: ask before a PR goes far past about 400 lines; wait for the leader's floor on a PR when it says it will re-run one; questions only the operator can answer go to the leader as an A/B choice.

The rest of #308, as you describe it, is within the ruling."
